recommendations.headline: Customer satisfaction, not price, is the biggest lever on winning business: satisfied calls convert at 72% versus just 10% for neutral calls (56% of all calls) and 2% for dissatisfied calls, while execution gaps like no fixed follow-up (380 calls) and no quote sent (227 calls) are keeping most calls stuck at 'callback' (1,173 of 2,141, 54.8%).
behaviour: Price-sensitive behaviour dominates: 423 calls show price_shopper behaviour, 241 are comparing_quotes, and price_high is the top objection (369 calls), but price is actually discussed in only 31.5% of calls (674/2141; 1,467 not_discussed).
Only 19% of calls (406/2141) end in an order while 54.8% (1,173) end in callback and 12.8% (275) stay unclear, showing heavy stalling behaviour.
Stock_availability (368 calls) is nearly as common a blocker as price_high (369) and needed by 415 customers, showing availability concerns rival pricing concerns.
Loyalty signals are weak: repeat_buyer appears in only 194 calls, loyal_to_us in just 10, and referral in 14, versus 1,117 dealer calls overall - the base is transactional, not sticky.
Urgent buyers (223) and bulk buyers (224) are sizeable segments but win rates by objection show transport_cost objections convert best (31%) while competitor_cheaper converts worst (7%, 85 calls).
satisfaction: Satisfaction is the strongest predictor of winning: satisfied calls (628, 29%) close at 72%, neutral calls (1,200, 56%) close at only 10%, and dissatisfied calls (217, 10%) close at just 2% - a 70-point swing driven by call quality, not price.

Most price conversations never reach resolution: 1,467 of 2,141 calls (68.5%) show price 'not_discussed', only 173 (8%) end in accepted price and 87 (4%) in too_high - reps are not closing the pricing loop.

Negative sentiment (372 calls, 17%) and dissatisfaction (217 calls, 10%) align with top rep misses - slow/unclear answers (376) and no fixed follow-up (380) - pointing to service experience, not rate, as the main irritant.

conversion.title: Convert neutral calls into satisfied ones
conversion.evidence: Neutral calls are 56% of volume (1,200/2,141) but win only 10% vs 72% for satisfied calls.
conversion.action: Give reps a call-closing checklist (confirm need, stock, rate, next step) to end every call on a clear, positive note rather than leaving it open.

conversion.title: Build a competitor rebuttal script
conversion.evidence: competitor_cheaper has the lowest win rate (7%, 85 calls) of all objections despite being less frequent than price_high.
conversion.action: Train reps to counter competitor price claims with stock reliability, quality certification and service speed instead of offering to match rates on the spot.

conversion.title: Enforce fixed follow-ups and fast quote delivery
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed (380) and no_quote_sent (227) are the top two rep misses; 54.8% of calls end as callback.
conversion.action: Mandate every call ends with a named follow-up date/time logged in CRM and a WhatsApp/email quote sent within a fixed turnaround (e.g., same day).

conversion.title: Resolve stock-availability friction on the call
conversion.evidence: stock_availability objection (368 calls) wins only 15% of the time, nearly matching price_high (369 calls) in frequency.
conversion.action: Give reps real-time stock visibility and a standard 'offer closest alternative size/brand' script instead of 'let me check and call back.'

conversion.title: Explicitly ask for the order
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order was flagged 152 times while order_pct is only 19%.
conversion.action: Coach reps to always close with a direct order ask once stock and rate are confirmed.

conversion.title: Qualify 'unknown' segment callers early
conversion.evidence: Unknown segment accounts for 543 calls but wins only 15%, the lowest of all segments; didnt_ask_requirement flagged 53 times.
conversion.action: Require reps to capture segment, region and requirement details in the first minute of every new call for correct routing and follow-up.

conversion.title: Speed up and standardise price responses
conversion.evidence: slow_or_unclear_answer flagged 376 times against 672 price_enquiry intents.
conversion.action: Equip reps with an always-updated rate card/lookup tool so price questions are answered instantly and consistently.

offers.title: Cutting and processing service bundle
offers.for_whom: Fabricators and contractors needing cut-to-size material
offers.why: cutting_processing is needed in 216 calls and features in multiple recurring questions about cutting plates/channels.

offers.title: Priority/fast-track dispatch for urgent orders
offers.for_whom: Urgent buyers (223 calls) and high-urgency calls (315)
offers.why: fast_delivery is the 2nd most-cited need (386) and many won calls involved same-day loading requests.

offers.title: WhatsApp rate/stock update subscription
offers.for_whom: Dealers and price-shopper behaviour customers (423 calls)
offers.why: regular_updates need cited 270 times and many questions ask whether a previously sent rate was received.

offers.title: Quality assurance pack with test certificates
offers.for_whom: Industrial and contractor buyers handling specified projects
offers.why: quality_doubt objection seen 145 times (20% win) and test_certificate explicitly needed in 144 calls.

offers.title: Combined multi-item quoting (e.g., pipe+angle, TMT+plate)
offers.for_whom: Dealers and fabricators placing mixed-material orders
offers.why: Multiple customers ask for combined items on a single quote/order, a convenience currently handled ad hoc.

offers.title: Site-delivery service for project buyers
offers.for_whom: Contractors and builders (84 and 27 calls, win 27-30%)
offers.why: site_delivery need cited 100 times with several questions on delivering to sites 10-12 km away.

loyalty.title: Priority stock allocation during shortages
loyalty.how: Reserve a stock quota for repeat_buyer (194) and bulk_buyer (224) accounts ahead of general availability during tight supply periods
loyalty.why: stock_availability is a top-two objection (368 calls) and a likely cause of lost repeat business.

loyalty.title: Dedicated point-of-contact for top dealers
loyalty.how: Assign a named relationship rep to high-frequency dealer accounts (1,117 dealer calls, 33% win)
loyalty.why: Reduces no_follow_up_fixed misses (380) and builds continuity that the data shows is currently weak (only 10 loyal_to_us flags).

loyalty.title: Consider a structured credit-period pilot for vetted repeat accounts
loyalty.how: Evaluate offering limited, performance-based credit terms to customers with a proven payment history, reviewed periodically
loyalty.why: credit_terms objection appears in 85 calls and needs_credit/credit_period needs appear 101 and 73 times respectively.

loyalty.title: Formal referral recognition program
loyalty.how: Track referral-sourced leads and acknowledge/reward the referring customer
loyalty.why: Referral behaviour is recorded in only 14 calls, suggesting an untapped and currently unrewarded source of growth.

loyalty.title: Value-add perks for loyal/repeat customers
loyalty.how: Offer small non-price perks like free sample cuts, priority after-sales support, or faster complaint resolution to repeat_buyer and loyal_to_us customers
loyalty.why: after_sales_support is needed in 31 calls while loyal_to_us is flagged only 10 times, showing room to convert repeat buyers into advocates.

non_price_benefits.title: Stock depth and availability across sizes
non_price_benefits.why: stock_availability is the top customer need (415 mentions) and a leading objection (368 calls).

non_price_benefits.title: Fast or same-day dispatch capability
non_price_benefits.why: fast_delivery is the second most-cited need (386) and recurs in well-converted calls involving same-day loading.

non_price_benefits.title: In-house cutting and processing services
non_price_benefits.why: cutting_processing need cited 216 times across calls.

non_price_benefits.title: Quality assurance with test certificates
non_price_benefits.why: quality_doubt is a frequent objection (145 calls) and test_certificate is specifically requested 144 times.

non_price_benefits.title: Technical and sizing advice from experienced staff
non_price_benefits.why: needs_technical_help behaviour appears in 271 calls and technical_advice need in 160 calls, e.g., the well-handled ISMB vs NPP explanation.

non_price_benefits.title: Reliable, consistent supply relationship
non_price_benefits.why: consistent_supply need (164) and repeat_buyer behaviour (194) show customers value dependable ongoing supply over one-off deals.

top_questions.question: What is the current rate for this size/product?
top_questions.answer_tip: Quote clearly from an updated rate card immediately, stating what is included (GST, transport) rather than promising to check and call back.

top_questions.question: Can you match a competitor's rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Avoid committing to match; highlight stock reliability, certified quality and delivery speed, and offer to escalate a verified competitor quote to management.

top_questions.question: Is this size/brand available in stock?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check live stock status on the call; if unavailable, proactively suggest the closest available alternative instead of just promising to check.

top_questions.question: Will you offer credit terms, PDC, or a bank guarantee?
top_questions.answer_tip: State the standard payment policy clearly and offer to escalate long-term, high-volume customers for a case-by-case review.

top_questions.question: When will the material be dispatched or delivered?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a specific day/time window and confirm a follow-up update rather than an open-ended promise.

top_questions.question: Can you send the quote on WhatsApp/email?
top_questions.answer_tip: Send the quote during or immediately after the call so it isn't left as a pending task.

top_questions.question: Why did the rate change from the earlier quote?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain market/basic price movement transparently and mention the validity period of quotes going forward.

top_questions.question: Do you provide cutting or site delivery?
top_questions.answer_tip: Proactively confirm these capabilities early in the call as a differentiator, even if not directly asked.
